project.name: Mantine Dashboard Builder
project.summary: A dashboard builder that runs in the browser: an app frame around a canvas of charts, numbers and tables, fed by swappable data sources. A small helper server (the relay) runs the database queries a browser can't.

nodes.label: App and pages
nodes.summary: Starts the app, wires the shared pieces together and decides which page each web address shows; the only place features and plugins meet.
nodes.details: Tests and stories stay next to the code they check, in every part of this map. There is no separate Tests part.

nodes.label: Pages by address
nodes.summary: One file per web address (dashboards, data sources, integrations, settings, debug); each loads its data and hands it to a feature screen.

nodes.label: App frame
nodes.summary: The frame around every page: top bar, docking sidebar, docking context bar, breadcrumbs and the offline banner.

nodes.label: Top bar
nodes.summary: Search, the light/dark switch and the user menu along the top.

nodes.label: Sidebar
nodes.summary: The left menu of areas and pages, which can dock, collapse or float.

nodes.label: Context bar
nodes.summary: The right-hand panel with tabs about the current view: details, inspect, notifications.

nodes.label: Screens
nodes.summary: What people actually work with: dashboards, data connections, integrations, notifications and settings. Screens never use each other directly.

nodes.label: Dashboards
nodes.summary: The dashboard list and the dashboard page: viewing, searching and opening dashboards.

nodes.label: Dashboard loading
nodes.summary: Loads and saves dashboards and drafts, fetches each widget's data and refreshes it on a timer.

nodes.label: Open dashboard memory
nodes.summary: Remembers the open dashboard while it's edited, with undo and redo, and works out the time range in use.

nodes.label: Widget canvas
nodes.summary: The drag-and-resize grid of widget tiles, each tile's header and menu, and the keyboard shortcuts.

nodes.label: Dashboard toolbar
nodes.summary: Time range, refresh, edit buttons and JSON import and export at the top of a dashboard.

nodes.label: Widget editor
nodes.summary: Adding and changing widgets: the widget form, the query editor, placement and the leave-without-saving check.

nodes.label: Data connections
nodes.summary: Adding and testing database connections, the locked box that keeps their passwords, and choosing which data plugins go into the build.

nodes.label: Integrations
nodes.summary: The integrations page and the Sentry error-reporting setup and checks.

nodes.label: Settings and debug
nodes.summary: Appearance settings (theme, density, reduced motion) and a debug page that shows every message, error and loading state.

nodes.label: Notifications inbox
nodes.summary: The inbox of past messages shown as a context-bar tab.

nodes.label: Plugins
nodes.summary: The swappable parts: the rules every widget and data source follows, the built-in ones, and the optional database plugins chosen at build time.

nodes.label: Widgets
nodes.summary: The built-in widgets: time-series chart, KPI numbers and the large virtual table.

nodes.label: Built-in data sources
nodes.summary: Sample data and local JSON files, available without any connection.

nodes.label: Database plugins
nodes.summary: Optional data sources for AWS, Google, Azure SQL and MongoDB; the last two go through the relay.

nodes.label: Core rules
nodes.summary: Plain logic with no screens: what a dashboard and its layout look like, time ranges, the data table every widget reads, errors, the relay's message format and password encryption.

nodes.label: Design system
nodes.summary: The look of every screen: colour and size tokens, the Mantine theme, and shared building blocks such as pages, panels, split views and loading placeholders.

nodes.label: Building blocks
nodes.summary: Shared pieces used across screens: page, section, surface, split view, error and loading states.

nodes.label: Theme
nodes.summary: How each Mantine component looks by default here: buttons, inputs, menus, tabs, dialogs.

nodes.label: Tokens
nodes.summary: The named colours, spacing and sizes everything else must use.

nodes.label: App services
nodes.summary: Services every screen can use: messages and the inbox, Sentry error reporting, the password vault, saved preferences and small helpers.

nodes.label: Relay server
nodes.summary: A small server that runs SQL Server and MongoDB queries for the browser; it keeps nothing, the connection details come with each request.

nodes.label: Build and checks
nodes.summary: Everything that builds and checks the app rather than running in it: build and test settings, Storybook, lint rules, test helpers and the docs catalog.

nodes.label: Layer rules
nodes.summary: Custom lint rules that keep each layer importing only the layers below it, with tests proving every rule fires.

nodes.label: Test helpers
nodes.summary: Shared helpers for tests and stories: rendering with the app's providers, a test router and sample dashboards. Not the tests themselves, which sit beside their code.

nodes.label: Sentry
nodes.summary: Error and performance reporting.

nodes.label: AWS
nodes.summary: Athena, Aurora, Redshift and DynamoDB, queried straight from the browser.

nodes.label: Google Cloud
nodes.summary: BigQuery and Firestore, plus Google sign-in.

nodes.label: SQL Server / Azure SQL
nodes.summary: Databases reached only through the relay.

nodes.label: MongoDB
nodes.summary: Document databases reached only through the relay.

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.summary: Where Add to build edits the plugin list on the deployed site.

edges.label: query
edges.description: Azure SQL and MongoDB plugins send each query, with its connection details, to the relay at a configured address.

edges.label: shared contract
edges.description: The relay uses only the core rules, so the browser and the relay agree on one message format.

annotations.note: The single place built-in and optional plugins are registered.
The only contract between data sources and widgets.

flows.title: Open a dashboard
flows.description: From a web address to charts on screen.

steps.note: The dashboard address is read, including time range and edit mode.
The dashboard is loaded: a saved copy in this browser, or the sample file.
It's checked against the dashboard rules before anything is shown.
Tiles are laid out on the canvas.
Each tile asks its data source for rows.
The chart, KPI or table draws the rows.
Someone adds a connection; its password goes into the locked vault.
A widget's query goes to the Azure SQL plugin.
The relay runs the query, since browsers can't talk to SQL Server.
The database answers; rows come back as a data table.
